key_insight: CalArena shows that post-hoc calibration methods need standardized, large-scale evaluation, and that smooth, calibration-specific approaches consistently outperform simple binning-based methods.
engineering_relevance: For deployed ML systems that rely on trustworthy probabilities, the benchmark helps practitioners choose calibration methods that improve reliability without undermining predictive performance.
method: Aggregated nearly 2000 experiments across tabular and vision tasks, spanning binary, multiclass, and large-scale classification.
Benchmarked predictions from classical models, deep networks, and foundation models using a common reproducible framework.
Compared dozens of post-hoc calibration methods with Post-Hoc Improvement (PHI) in proper scoring rules as the primary evaluation criterion.
evidence_signal: The study compiles a large, standardized benchmark with nearly 2000 experiments and unified implementations across diverse datasets, models, and calibration settings.
watch_item: Results depend on the quality of the underlying predictions and on careful multiclass handling, so generic calibration methods may fail in high-dimensional settings.
paper_title: CalArena: A Large-Scale Post-Hoc Calibration Benchmark
